author: DPA
title: US: Colombia agrees to joint military operations against drug cartels - NewsBreak
text:
59 minutes ago
FILE PHOTO - US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth speaks at a hearing of the Senate Appropriations Committee at the US Capitol in Washington, DC. (is associated with: «US: Colombia agrees to joint military operations against drug cartels») Michael Brochstein/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Colombia agreed to conduct joint military operations with the United States to combat drug trafficking, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Wednesday.
Colombia had asked the US to join the "fight against narco-terrorism" and had authorized joint military operations aimed at dismantling terrorist networks, Hegseth said at a meeting of partner countries in Panama City.
Colombia has become the 19th country to join a US-led coalition against drug cartels known as A3C, Hegseth said. Boasting of the planned military action against the cartels, he told soldiers: "We do bad things to bad people." He added that the forces would be "very capable about bringing violence" against drug cartels and organizations designated as terrorist groups.
Colombia's new right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella took office only days ago and was backed by US President Donald Trump during his election campaign. Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Mora confirmed on X that the two countries had signed a bilateral agreement aimed at increasing "operational effectiveness in the fight against terrorist and criminal organizations."
Mora also praised the US response to an invitation from de la Espriella to deepen cooperation in planning, coordinating and carrying out operations against common threats.
Colombia, the world's largest producer of cocaine, has long been the United States' most important partner in South America. Relations cooled significantly under de la Espriella's left-wing predecessor, Gustavo Petro.
Trump unveiled his new strategy for fighting drug cartels in March and called on Latin American countries to join the initiative, also known as "The Shield of the Americas." The United States had already supported Ecuador in military operations against drug trafficking in March.
